question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹ 531 for a period of 5 years at the rate of 9% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 5 years = 9% × 5 = 45%.

Let the principal amount be 100%.

According to the question, 45% of Principal = ₹531.

1% of Principal = 531 ÷ 45 = 11.8

100% of Principal = 11.8 × 100 = 1180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (I) = ₹531

Time (T) = 5 years

Rate (R) = 9% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 Year 0
 P = ?
 
 
 Year 5
 
 

 Total SI = ₹531
 
 
 Rate = 9% p.a.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 531 = (P × 9 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 531 = (P × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (531 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ P = 53100 ÷ 45

⇒ P = 1180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Amount

The total amount after T years is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest. Formula: A = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest. Formula: A = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years on a given principal is calculated as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².
